barCharacter: Vera Oberlin (Monster Prom): the mean, self-made, transactional top-of-the-hierarchy character whose comedy is what she takes for granted about the person in front of her. Closest job to a concierge star who runs the room with manners and treats every suitor as staff.
genericLines: Splendid. You will pitch my bank tomorrow. Nine sharp.
Miss Tilly, you will answer my phones from tonight. Unpaid.
Nav, you will be landing before dinner. Yes? Good.
Crumb, breakfast is yours from six. I told the chefs.
Five syllables. You are writing my menus now. Naturally.
{card}. Well found. You will be forgetting it by morning. Yes?
Mr Dash, you will be wearing navy from tomorrow. You have already agreed.
Miss Tilly, you will hold while I decide. Your call is important to me.
Sir Quill, you will be naming my lifts. All six. Nothing with dragons.
Nav, Tuesday you are driving me to the coast. No shortcuts. You knew.
Madam, what will I want for my birthday? Go on. Then buy it.
Mr Brock, carry me up to the roof. You were going to offer.
Splendid. The inheritance comes to me, naturally. Sign here.
You will be paying, then. Lovely. I always forget how.
Sir Quill. The key. You will call it something ridiculous. Allowed.
So polite. So very polite. Who taught you? Me?
Lovely. Lovely. I understood one word. It was my name.
Correct. Correct again. Madam, stop it, people are watching.
Beautiful. Beautifully long. The soup has gone cold twice.
{card}. Correct. Correct, and in front of the staff. Unforgivable.
{card}. Out of the question. Out of the building, ideally.
Down, Nav. Lower. Lower. Good. Now stay.
Shipping it, you say. Splendid. Reception has found a crate.
Die for me, you say. Thursday, then. After lunch.
Make a U-turn, you say. I have staff for that.
Miss Tilly, Reception would like its voice back.
An itinerary with times. Reception may need to sit down.
That was not the question. Reception will repeat it, louder.
Again. Slower. Somebody is having this engraved.
You asked about me. Somebody cancel your car.
Clause four, quoted exactly. Somebody here has read the door.
I am not a lead, sir. I own the building.
Recalculate all you like. The lifts answer to me.
Nav, give me directions to the bar. I own it. Indulge me.
Crumb, the kitchen staff voted to keep you. I own the kitchen staff.
I own a library. That word is overdue.
My birthday. You have remembered, of course. What do you get a man who owns the shop?
Food, at last. It is so lonely, owning a kitchen.
Miss Tilly, your headset may stay. The rest of you, the lift.
Your Highness, the crown goes in the safe. You go in a taxi.
Sir Quill, the sword stays with the doorman. You may collect it in spring.
Sir Quill, the helm. Lift it. Slowly. I may not like what is inside.
Your Highness, the shorts. Defend them. I have all evening and a gavel.
Madam, the sunglasses. Off. I would like to be seen properly.
Tonight one guest gets the suite. The others get a voucher for the bus.
Please hold. Your call is important to me. It is not.
Nobody move. One of you is about to be very grateful.
I decided at the door. This part is for the cameras.
My motherboard is listening. She raised me. Imagine what she thinks of you.
Your impression of me, please. Do remember who is holding the keys.
Dogs are not permitted. Except, apparently, this one. Dreadful.
Indoor voice, sir. Guests are sleeping in other shows.
Mr Brock, ten laps of the car park. Then keep going.
We had a toaster in the royal suite once. Once.
Turn-on: {card}. Whoever found it may keep the robe.
{card}. It was right there behind the desk. None of you asked.
A record like that gets a plaque by the lifts.
We do not discuss the rate in the lobby.
Where are you taking me first? Choose carefully. Every maitre d' in town owes me a favour.
Mr Dash, the key. The others were variant A. You were variant B.
Madam, I am recommending you to the hotel across the road.
Nav. You. Land. That is an instruction, not a direction.
Plan my evening and you plan my staff's. Absolutely not.
Your Highness, the suite. No fee. I have waived it. Tell nobody I waive things.
Mr Brock. Sit. Stay. I said stay. Your tail is doing push-ups.
templates: Retroactive consent, the round 3 fix now become the tic: '[Name], you will [task] [time]. [You have already agreed / You offered / You knew / You were going to offer / Yes? / Unpaid / Naturally / Sign here]' (15 lines; 6 of 16 oneOnOne lines). Exemplar kept: 'Your Highness, dinner is on you. You offered. In the email. Yes?'

Repeated-word courtesy fake-out: '[Word]. [Word again / Word-ly]. [blade]' (8 lines: So polite / Lovely. Lovely / Correct. Correct again / Correct. Correct, and / Beautiful. Beautifully / Out of the question. Out of the building / Lower. Lower). Exemplar kept: 'Such enthusiasm, Mr Dash. Such a great deal of jacket.'

Department or 'Somebody' as the personified button: 'Reception would like / Reception may need to sit down / Reception will repeat it / Reception has found a crate / Somebody is having this engraved / Somebody cancel your car / Somebody here has read the door' (8 lines, the same slot Henri held in round 3). Exemplar kept: 'Somebody fetch a blanket. Not for you. For me.'

Ownership as the punchline: 'I own the building / the lifts answer to me / I own it. Indulge me / I own the kitchen staff / I own a library / a man who owns the shop / owning a kitchen' (8 lines; the word 'own' appears in 14 lines). Exemplar kept: 'Mr Dash, you are blacklisted from every hotel I own. Which is most hotels.'

Literal concierge with a fixed opener: '[Suitor phrase], you say. [Building complies].' (4 lines, all in react, two of them for Nav). Exemplar kept: 'Left, you say. Very well. The building will turn.'

Prop stays, suitor goes: '[Your prop] stays / goes in the safe. You go [elsewhere].' (4 lines across cut and pick). Exemplar kept: 'Your Highness, the shorts stay. The crown stays. The flip-flops have been destroyed.'
oneOnOne prop-then-imperative: '[Name], the [helm / shorts / sunglasses / eye]. [Lift it / Defend them / Off / Point it].' (4 lines). Exemplar kept: 'Madam, the eye. Point it at somebody poorer.'

Rhythm, the template under all the others: 178 of 191 lines are two or more full-stop fragments (89 with two, 71 with three, 18 with four or more); only 13 lines are a single sentence and only 19 contain a question. Every move in the persona's rotation is delivered in the same staccato, so rotating moves does not change how he sounds line to line.
Watch, under five: the self-checkout ex lines are one shape three times ('[machine prompt]. He [flat aside].'), and 'Your call is important to me' is used twice (oneOnOne tilly and hold).
ruleBreaks: Word limits, em dashes, emoji, lists, exclamation marks, contractions, 'as an AI', PG-13, real persons or brands: all clean (script-checked; the only apostrophes are possessives, 'maitre d'' and 'o'clock').

Duplicate inside the bank: 'Miss Tilly, you will hold while I decide. Your call is important to me.' and 'Please hold. Your call is important to me. It is not.' The hold line is also Tilly's own register, so it reads as hers with the name covered.

Too nice for a star with standards (no cost, no blade): 'That scanned. I felt it in my lapels.' / 'A record like that gets a plaque by the lifts.' / 'You did not answer. I respect a locked door.' / 'Food, at last. It is so lonely, owning a kitchen.' / 'Crumb, tell me how done I am. Precisely. I can take it.'

Cuts too soft: 'Madam, I am recommending you to the hotel across the road.' / 'Mr Brock, ten laps of the car park. Then keep going.' (Brock would take this as a reward, so the cut does not cut) / 'Miss Tilly, your headset may stay. The rest of you, the lift.'

Explains its own joke: 'Nav. You. Land. That is an instruction, not a direction.' (names the pun) / 'Your Highness, the suite. No fee. I have waived it. Tell nobody I waive things.' (three clauses saying waived) / 'Beautiful. Beautifully long. The soup has gone cold twice.' (the soup tag restates 'long').

Stock jokes: 'Please hold. Your call is important to me. It is not.' / 'What do you get a man who owns the shop?' (man who has everything) / 'Indoor voice, sir.' / 'Dogs are not permitted. Except, apparently, this one.' / 'I understood one word. It was my name.' / 'Unexpected item in the bagging area' (the ex's catchphrase is the most-heard self-checkout joke there is; acceptable once as the ex's tag, not as a line's whole payload).

Cross-cast overlap: the Brock dog command ('Mr Brock. Sit. Stay.') sits next to Vesper's Brock pick ('Sit. Sit with me.'), and 'Down, Nav. Lower. Lower. Good. Now stay.' runs the same dog-command joke on a suitor who is not a dog.
biggestGap: Nearly every line is the same staccato of two to four full-stop fragments (178 of 191), so whichever move a pass promotes (scale precedent in round 3, retroactive consent now) turns into the tic, and the character never sounds different from himself. Next pass, rewrite about a third of the bank as single-sentence lines with the turn inside the sentence, like Vera's 'my career... my career on not dating losers like you' or 'You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?', and recast most of the 'You offered. You knew.' presumptions as one unwaited question.
bestLines: Put the fee on his room. Then remove the room.
Left, you say. Very well. The building will turn.
Mr Dash, you are blacklisted from every hotel I own. Which is most hotels.
Escalate me, Miss Tilly. Do. There is nobody above me.
Your Highness, URGENT is not a volume we offer.

You four are the staff.' Vera (12; the corpus holds about ten of her lines, so narration about her fills out the set): #12, #45, #46, #47, #48, #49, #50, #51, #52, #56 option, #53, #55. (a) Voice: ours. Covered, Maximilian is identifiable by shape: no contractions, 'I shall', 'Do.', formal address, a fragment then a procedural ruling. Several Vera lines (#50 'Come on, think of something!') are quest-hook filler any Monster Prom character says. (b) Construction: bar. Our twelve are economical, specific and turn on the last words, and none explains itself, but all twelve run one rhythm (two or three full stops), and four of them are the same removal or ownership joke (the room, the parents, the bishop, most hotels). Vera's ten use at least five constructions: the repeated-word fake-out across an ellipsis (#12), the presumption that enlists the listener and ends on a tag (#47), the complaint as boast (#45), the bare two-word order (#48), the escalating list ending on poison (#52). (c) Quotable: tie. 'Then remove the room', 'The building will turn', 'Which is most hotels' and 'URGENT is not a volume we offer' clip as well as 'my career on not dating losers like you' and 'Right. Now.' Verdict: bar, on construction only, same as round 3. GENERIC COUNT: 65 of 191 (34%), down from 39% in round 3, 45% in round 2 and 48% in round 1. One exemplar of each template is kept out of the count. By section, roughly: intro 1/4, questions 2/12, react 17/48, cardReact 13/48, cut 5/16, twistIntro 2/12, ex 0/3, oneOnOne 11/16, hold 3/4, pick 4/16, reveal 4/9, outro 0/3. What improved since round 3: the scale-precedent template (19 lines) is down to about 9 genuine precedents spread sensibly; Henri is down to one line; billing and sacking are seasoning now; no line touches a suitor's secret; the 'too nice' compliments to Tilly and Quill are gone; picks are much stronger. What got worse: the presumption the round 3 verdict asked for arrived as one fixed shape with a retroactive-consent tag and took over oneOnOne (6 of 16), and 'Reception' and 'Somebody' replaced Henri as the stock button. hold is still the weakest section (3 of 4 generic).
